title: Triggers and Events
subtitle: push, pull_request, schedule, workflow_dispatch, paths, and branches filters

content.text: Every way to trigger a workflow

content.code:
on:

  # ── Code events ────────────────────────────────────────

  # Push to specific branches
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - 'release/**'      # wildcard: release/1.0, release/2.0
      - '!dev/**'         # ! = exclude this pattern
    tags:
      - 'v*'              # any tag starting with v (v1.0, v2.3.1)
    paths:
      - 'src/**'          # only trigger if src/ files changed
      - '!src/**/*.test.ts'  # but NOT test files

  # Pull request events
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]   # default
    branches: [main]

  # ── Manual triggers ─────────────────────────────────────

  # Manual run from GitHub UI or API
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Deploy target'
        required: true
        default: 'staging'
        type: choice
        options: [staging, production]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Dry run only (no actual deploy)'
        type: boolean
        default: false

  # Called by another workflow
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      image_tag:
        required: true
        type: string

  # ── Scheduled triggers ──────────────────────────────────

  # Cron syntax (UTC): daily at 2:30am
  schedule:
    - cron: '30 2 * * *'        # daily at 2:30 UTC
    - cron: '0 9 * * 1'         # every Monday at 9am UTC

  # ── Other useful events ─────────────────────────────────

  release:
    types: [published]     # runs when a GitHub Release is published

  issues:
    types: [opened]        # run on new issue

  repository_dispatch:     # external HTTP call triggers this
    types: [deploy]

# ── Pattern 1: PR check (validate before merge) ──────────
name: PR Check
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm ci && npm test

---
# ── Pattern 2: Deploy on push to main ────────────────────
name: Deploy
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: ./deploy.sh

---
# ── Pattern 3: Nightly dependency audit ─────────────────
name: Security Audit
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'   # 6am UTC daily
jobs:
  audit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm audit --audit-level=high

---
# ── Pattern 4: Only run when relevant files change ───────
name: Backend CI
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'server/**'
      - 'packages/api/**'
      - '!**/*.md'        # ignore markdown changes

name: Manual Deploy
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        type: choice
        options: [staging, production]
        required: true
      image_tag:
        description: 'Docker image tag to deploy'
        required: true
        default: 'latest'

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: ${{ inputs.environment }}  # requires manual approval if set up
    steps:
      - name: Deploy
        run: |
          echo "Deploying tag: ${{ inputs.image_tag }}"
          echo "Target: ${{ inputs.environment }}"
          ./scripts/deploy.sh \
            --env ${{ inputs.environment }} \
            --tag ${{ inputs.image_tag }}

content.text: Use paths filtering to speed up monorepos. In a monorepo with frontend and backend packages, add paths: ['server/**'] to the backend workflow so backend CI only runs when backend files change. Without this, a README fix in the frontend triggers the entire backend test suite — wasting minutes of CI time on every commit.

questions.question: You want a workflow to run tests on every PR, but deploy only when code is pushed to main. How do you configure this?
options: Create two separate workflow files — one for PR (pull_request trigger), one for deploy (push: branches: [main] trigger)
Use a single file with 'on: push' and add an 'if: github.ref == main' condition on the deploy job
Either of the above work — separate files is cleaner; if-conditions work in one file
You must use workflow_call to link them
questions.explanation: Both approaches work. Separate files (ci.yml and deploy.yml) is cleaner and more maintainable. A single file with job-level if conditions works too. The separate-file approach is preferred for most teams because each workflow has a clear single purpose and separate status checks in GitHub's PR UI.

faq.q: How do I trigger a workflow from another workflow?
faq.a: Two ways: (1) workflow_call — defines a reusable workflow that other workflows call with 'uses: ./.github/workflows/shared.yml'. (2) repository_dispatch — one workflow makes an HTTP POST to the GitHub API to trigger another. workflow_call is preferred for same-repo orchestration.

examples: on: release: types: [published] — publishes an npm package automatically when a GitHub Release is created; used by most open-source npm packages
on: schedule: cron — used for nightly database backups, dependency vulnerability scans, and freshness checks on links/APIs
